feature: The smallest and largest a container may get
summary: A group that is the size of its contents can now be given a floor and a ceiling on each axis, so a button with one letter in it is still a button and a card with a very long title stops growing instead of running off the screen.
setup: Photonz Next, release Next in the Experiments window, flag next-auto-layout on (it is on by default). Nothing new to turn on.

try.do: Open the component shelf and drop the starter Button on the canvas.
Show the inspector and find the Layout section. Click the chevron beside the word Width.
Type 200 into Smallest and press Return.
Double click the button's word, shorten it to OK, press Return and click away. The pill stays 200 wide.
Empty the Smallest box and press Return, then type 56 into Largest.
Empty Largest, then click the chevron beside Height and type 72 into its Smallest.
Set Arrangement to Stack, then back to Free, and check the numbers are still there.
Save the document, close it and open it again.

evaluate: Is a chevron beside Width the right place to keep these, or should the two numbers always be on screen?
When a floor holds the button open, the word centres in the room it made. Is that what you expected, or should it stay put where it was?
A word wider than its ceiling overhangs the right edge. Is overhanging the honest answer, or should the pill clip it?
The Width row still says Hug while a limit is holding the box. Does that read as wrong to you?
Are Smallest and Largest the right words, or do you want Min and Max?
rough: There is no way to make words wrap or shrink when they outgrow a ceiling, so they overhang. That is the next thing this feature wants.
A screen cannot be given limits: its box is its own frame, so the rows are hidden there, the same as Width and Height already are.
Type a fixed width of 400 with a ceiling of 200 and the W field says 400 while the box is 200. The section's sentence says why, but the two numbers do disagree on screen.
Nothing in the mock drew these at all. The whole shape comes from the hug audit's own complaint, so there was nothing to copy and nothing to argue with.
Screen Recording was granted for this run, so both pictures are real window captures, not offscreen renders.
